parts.name: Understand concepts
parts.question: What is a multi-region platform, what can a region provide, and what do applications need?
parts.summary: Four connectivity profiles describe the platform options. Four archetypes describe what applications require.

parts.name: Qualify regions
parts.question: Can this region support the workloads we expect?
parts.summary: Four checks lead to one of four outcomes: excluded, candidate, conditional, or qualified.

parts.name: Select the regional design
parts.question: What should the platform provide in a qualified region?
parts.summary: Make three choices from short lists: the connectivity profile, where each shared service is provided, and whether the hybrid connectivity you already have is reused.

parts.name: Prepare the region
parts.question: What has to exist before workloads arrive?
parts.summary: Build only what the selected design calls for, through the automation you already run. Two of the four profiles need no hub.

parts.name: Place workloads
parts.question: Should this workload use the region now?
parts.summary: Decide per workload, with current evidence.

checks.name: Business and geography
checks.question: Where do we need Azure presence?
checks.decision: Confirm that the region has sufficient business value to justify deeper assessment.

checks.name: Data and compliance
checks.question: Are we allowed to operate here?
checks.decision: Exclude a region when it cannot satisfy a mandatory data, compliance, or policy requirement.

checks.name: Workload requirements and dependencies
checks.question: What workload requirements and dependencies must the region support?
checks.decision: Identify and record the workload-driven platform requirements.

checks.name: Regional capability and availability
checks.question: Which regions can support the identified workload requirements?
checks.decision: Qualify candidate regions, documenting conditions, constraints, and unresolved validations.
checks.ifNotMet: Conditional, or excluded if the gap is mandatory.

outcomes.name: Excluded
outcomes.text: A mandatory requirement cannot be satisfied.

outcomes.name: Candidate
outcomes.text: The region is potentially viable, but additional discovery or validation is required before qualification.

outcomes.name: Conditional
outcomes.text: Current evidence supports the defined workload requirements if one or more documented conditions are resolved.

outcomes.name: Qualified as of the assessment date
outcomes.text: Current evidence supports the defined workload requirements, platform ownership is established, and workload-onboarding revalidation is still required.

choices.name: Connectivity profile
choices.select: One of four: Disconnected Spokes, Remote Hub Connected, Minimal Regional Hub, or Full Regional Hub.

choices.name: Shared-service placement
choices.select: For each shared service the workloads depend on: local, remote, or global.

choices.name: Hybrid connectivity
choices.select: Reuse the existing foundation, change it, or confirm that none is required.

drivers.name: Service, AI model, SKU, and quota availability
Datacenter and connectivity events
triggers: New Azure region in the geography

driversFigure.title: Common drivers of multi-region platform discussions
driversFigure.openText: They do not determine the regional architecture or the workload-placement outcome.
driversFigure.captionRight: Six common drivers and their typical triggers

scenarios.title: Regulated bank adopts a new in-country region
scenarios.situation: A financial-services organization operates workloads outside its home country. A new Azure region opens in-country while regulatory or business requirements create a need for certain data or services to remain there.

steps.label: Driver
steps.text: Data residency and regulatory requirements; new in-country Azure region.

steps.label: Deciding checks
steps.text: Check 2 confirms mandatory location requirements. Check 3 identifies affected workloads and dependencies. Check 4 validates required services, zones, access, and constraints.

steps.label: Qualification
steps.text: Qualified for defined Hybrid-Connected requirements; other portfolio workloads remain candidates until dependencies are understood.

steps.label: Archetype
steps.text: Hybrid-Connected Applications.

steps.label: Connectivity profile
steps.text: Minimal Regional Hub where selected local capabilities are required; existing hybrid connectivity reused where reachability and resiliency permit.

steps.label: Placement
steps.text: In-scope workloads relocate selectively; others remain in place. Recovery architecture stays workload-specific.

scenarios.takeaway: A new in-country region can be qualified for defined workload requirements without forcing portfolio-wide relocation. If the new region is nonpaired, design the recovery path explicitly (Appendix A).

short.situation: A new Azure region opens in-country while regulation requires certain data or services to remain there.
steps: Data residency and regulation; new in-country region.
Check 2 mandatory location; Check 3 affected workloads; Check 4 services, zones, access.
Qualified for Hybrid-Connected requirements; other workloads candidates.
Hybrid-Connected Applications.
Minimal Regional Hub; reuse existing hybrid connectivity where it permits.
In-scope workloads relocate selectively; recovery stays workload-specific.
short.takeaway: Qualify for defined requirements without forcing portfolio-wide relocation; if the new region is nonpaired, design the recovery path explicitly (Appendix A).

scenarios.title: AI team requires a specific model or GPU SKU
scenarios.situation: A product team requires an AI model, GPU SKU, or related Azure service that is unavailable in the organization’s existing regions or constrained by quota.

steps.label: Driver
steps.text: AI model, service, SKU, or quota availability.

steps.label: Deciding checks
steps.text: Check 1 confirms the business requirement. Check 2 validates data and compliance constraints. Check 4 validates current model, service, SKU, zone, access, and quota support.

steps.label: Qualification
steps.text: Qualified for the defined AI workload requirements; conditional for requirements that depend on private connectivity until that design is known and validated.

steps.label: Archetype
steps.text: Isolated Cloud-Native or AI where self-contained; Connected Cloud-Native or AI where private enterprise dependencies are required.

steps.label: Connectivity profile
steps.text: Disconnected Spokes where the workload is self-contained; a connected profile only where actual dependencies justify it.

steps.label: Placement
steps.text: Net-new deployment. Revalidate model, SKU, service, regional access, and quota at decision time.

scenarios.takeaway: Qualify against the requirements that exist today; do not introduce enterprise connectivity or regional platform capabilities before a workload requirement justifies them.

short.situation: The model, SKU, or service is unavailable in existing regions or constrained by quota.
steps: AI model, service, SKU, or quota availability.
Check 1 business need; Check 2 data constraints; Check 4 model, SKU, zone, access, quota.
Qualified for the AI requirements; conditional where private connectivity is not yet designed.
Isolated Cloud-Native or AI; Connected where private dependencies exist.
Disconnected Spokes; connected only where dependencies justify it.
Net-new; revalidate model, SKU, access, quota at decision time.
short.takeaway: Do not introduce enterprise connectivity or regional platform capabilities before a workload requirement justifies them.

scenarios.title: Acquisition brings an estate in another geography
scenarios.situation: An acquisition introduces a portfolio of interdependent applications, shared data, and local users in a geography where the organization has little or no existing Azure platform presence.

steps.label: Driver
steps.text: Business expansion through acquisition.

steps.label: Deciding checks
steps.text: Check 1 confirms the business need. Check 2 evaluates local data obligations. Check 3 maps portfolio-level dependencies, shared services, and connectivity requirements.

steps.label: Qualification
steps.text: Candidate while material dependencies remain unknown; qualified against defined portfolio requirements once discovery is complete.

steps.label: Archetype
steps.text: Interconnected Application Portfolios.

steps.label: Connectivity profile
steps.text: Remote Hub Connected where cross-region dependencies are acceptable; Minimal Regional Hub where east-west traffic, shared services, latency, or independence justify it.

steps.label: Placement
steps.text: Workloads remain in place initially and relocate selectively as business and integration requirements become known.

scenarios.takeaway: Aggregate portfolio dependencies determine the appropriate regional connectivity profile; application count or acquisition status does not.

short.situation: Interdependent applications, shared data, and local users where there is little Azure presence.
steps: Business expansion through acquisition.
Check 1 business need; Check 2 local data obligations; Check 3 portfolio dependencies.
Candidate until dependencies are known; then qualified.
Interconnected Application Portfolios.
Remote Hub Connected; Minimal Regional Hub where east-west or independence justify it.
Remain in place initially; relocate selectively with integration.
short.takeaway: Aggregate portfolio dependencies determine the profile; application count or acquisition status does not.

scenarios.title: Datacenter exit accelerates migration
scenarios.situation: A colocation contract is ending. Hybrid-connected applications must leave the datacenter, and the organization asks whether the event also requires adoption of another Azure region.

steps.label: Driver
steps.text: Datacenter and connectivity event.

steps.label: Deciding checks
steps.text: Check 3 identifies what must move together. Part 3 validates hybrid connectivity, datacenter and user geography, reachability, resiliency, and whether existing connectivity suffices.

steps.label: Qualification
steps.text: The existing target region remains qualified for the identified requirements; an additional region remains a candidate for future use.

steps.label: Archetype
steps.text: Hybrid-Connected Applications.

steps.label: Connectivity profile
steps.text: No new profile. Continue to use the existing strategic geographic hub where it satisfies requirements; no new regional hub solely because another region is available.

steps.label: Placement
steps.text: Most workloads land in the existing qualified region. Revisit the additional option when requirements change.

scenarios.takeaway: Remaining in an existing qualified region is a valid outcome. An additional region can remain an option rather than automatically becoming a deployment project.

short.situation: Hybrid-connected applications must leave a colocation facility; is another region now required?
steps: Datacenter and connectivity event.
Check 3 what moves together; Part 3 hybrid connectivity, reachability, resiliency.
Existing target region qualified; additional region a candidate.
Hybrid-Connected Applications.
No new profile: the existing strategic hub is reused.
Most workloads land in the existing qualified region.
short.takeaway: Remaining in an existing qualified region is a valid outcome; an additional region can stay an option, not a project.

misconceptions.claim: Adding a region means another landing-zone project, with its own governance model.
misconceptions.correction: The landing zone you already run is reused: governance, identity, policy, automation, and the operating model stay the same. A new region adds regional configuration and only the connectivity profile its workloads need.

misconceptions.claim: We must choose the perfect regions up front.
misconceptions.correction: Regional requirements and Azure capabilities change. Design the platform so additional qualified options can be introduced without redesigning the broader operating model.

misconceptions.claim: Qualified means approved for any workload.
misconceptions.correction: Qualification is scoped to defined requirements and evidence at a point in time. Each workload revalidates regional suitability during onboarding.

misconceptions.claim: Every new region needs a Full Regional Hub.
misconceptions.correction: Select the most efficient profile that satisfies the identified requirements. Profiles are not maturity stages; any profile can remain the long-term target while it continues to meet those requirements.

misconceptions.claim: Another Azure region requires another ExpressRoute circuit.
misconceptions.correction: An additional region does not by itself require another circuit. Additional hybrid connectivity should be introduced where reachability, diversity, failure-domain, latency, routing, or bandwidth requirements justify it.

misconceptions.claim: Enabling a region means migrating workloads.
misconceptions.correction: Regional qualification and platform readiness are not workload placement. Remaining in the existing region can be the appropriate outcome.

misconceptions.claim: A paired region is our disaster recovery.
misconceptions.correction: Region pairing supports specific Azure platform and service behaviors; it does not automatically provide workload recovery. Recovery must still be designed and validated per workload.
The platform creates regional options. Whether a workload is single-region, primary/recovery, or active across regions is a separate workload-specific resiliency decision.

gettingStarted.title: Name the drivers
gettingStarted.text: Identify what is prompting the discussion: business growth, regulation, service or SKU availability, resiliency, a datacenter or connectivity event, cost, or another measurable requirement.
gettingStarted.short: Business growth, regulation, service or SKU availability, resiliency, a datacenter or connectivity event, cost, or another measurable requirement.

gettingStarted.title: Understand the concepts
gettingStarted.text: Learn how a multi-region platform differs from a multi-region workload, the four connectivity profiles a region can provide, and the four Workload Landing Zone archetypes that describe what applications need. You make no decisions here. You learn the terms the next steps use.
gettingStarted.short: Platform versus workload, the four connectivity profiles, and the four Workload Landing Zone archetypes. No decisions yet.

gettingStarted.title: Shortlist and qualify candidate regions
gettingStarted.text: Work through the four qualification checks. Start with the two that need no technical assessment, business and geography and data and compliance, and remove regions that cannot satisfy mandatory conditions. For the regions that remain, identify workload requirements and dependencies, then validate regional capability and availability. Record each option as excluded, candidate, conditional, or qualified for the defined requirements, with evidence and revalidation triggers.
gettingStarted.short: Four checks. Start with business and geography, then data and compliance. Record each option as excluded, candidate, conditional, or qualified.

gettingStarted.title: Select the regional design
gettingStarted.text: For each qualified region, select the most efficient connectivity profile that meets the requirements, decide where each shared service is provided, and confirm whether the hybrid connectivity you already have is enough. Write the three choices into the regional design record, and agree who owns each decision.
gettingStarted.short: The most efficient connectivity profile, where each shared service is provided, and whether existing hybrid connectivity is enough. Write the regional design record.

gettingStarted.title: Prepare the region
gettingStarted.text: Build what the record says, through the automation you already run. Read only the page for the profile you selected: Disconnected Spokes, Remote Hub Connected, Minimal Regional Hub, or Full Regional Hub. Use the platform readiness checklist to confirm the region is ready before the first workload arrives.
gettingStarted.short: Build what the record says through the automation you already run. Confirm with the platform readiness checklist.

gettingStarted.title: Place the first workload
gettingStarted.text: Apply the workload-placement process using current evidence. Revalidate regional capabilities at decision time, govern the placement and resiliency decisions, and feed newly discovered requirements or platform gaps back into regional qualification.
gettingStarted.short: Apply the placement process with current evidence. Feed new requirements and platform gaps back into qualification.
